To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glucose responding neuronal activity in the LHA is increased by ghrelin and that in the pPVN and VMH is inhibited.
ghrelin increases the activity of glucose-sensitive lateral hypothalamic neurons (LHANs), but decreases that of ventromedial (VMH) and parvocellular (pPVN) hypothalamic neurons.
ghrelin modulates the activity of glucose sensitive neurons in the hypothalamus, which are involved in the orexinigenic actions of the hormone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ghrelin on the hypothalamic glucose sensitive neurons.
the effects of ghrelin on the hypothalamic glucose responsive neurons.
the effects of ghrelin on hypothalamic GSNs and GRNs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the orexigenicity of ghrelin may be exerted through the modulation of the activity of the GSNs and GRNs.
the orexigenicity of ghrelin may be mediated through both ARC- and hypothalamic glucose responsive neurons.
ghrelin is a potent orexigenic peptide and that the glucose sensing neurons in the hypothalamus may be involved in the orexic actions of ghrein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ghrelin may be an important factor for the control of food intake through the hypothalamic glucose sensing neurons.
ghrelin stimulates the activity of GSNs in the LHA and inhibits the activities of GSNs and GRNs in the pPVN and the VMH, respectively.
ghrelin is involved in the regulation of glucose metabolism in the brain, which is important for energy homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ghrelin receptor is expressed in the ARC, LHA and pPVN and that ghrelin stimulates food intake by acting on neurons in all three areas, but that it has a greater effect on neurons in the ARC than in the LHA or pPVN.
ghrelin has a direct stimulatory effect on the activity of GSNs in the LHA and an inhibitory effect on that of GRNs in the VMH and pPVN.
the glucose sensitive neurons in the LHI, VMH and pPVN play an important role in the orexigenc actions of ghrelins in hypothalamic circuits.
